column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.

it:essere:verb|Verbs of movement and change, and every reflexive verb, make the passato prossimo with essere: "sono andato", "sono nato", "mi sono alzato".|With essere the participle agrees with the subject: "lei è andata".
it:avere:verb|Age uses avere: "ho vent'anni". Also avere fame, avere sete, avere freddo, avere paura.|
it:camera:noun|Camera means room or bedroom. A camera is "macchina fotografica".|
it:fattoria:noun|Fattoria means farm, not factory (fabbrica).|
it:libreria:noun|A libreria is a bookshop or a bookcase. A library is "biblioteca".|
it:parente:noun|Parente means relative. Parents are "genitori".|
it:attualmente:adverb|Means currently, not actually. "Actually" is "in realtà".|
it:morbido:adjective|Morbido means soft, not morbid.|
it:magazzino:noun|Magazzino means warehouse or storeroom. A magazine is "rivista".|
it:sensibile:adjective|Means sensitive. "Sensible" in English is "ragionevole".|
it:simpatico:adjective|Simpatico means nice, likeable. Sympathetic (showing pity) is "comprensivo".|
it:piacere:verb|Piacere works backwards: the thing you like is the subject. "Mi piace la pizza", "mi piacciono i libri".|
it:sapere:verb|Sapere is for facts and skills ("so nuotare"), conoscere for people and places ("conosco Roma").|
it:conoscere:verb|Conoscere is for people and places; for facts and skills use sapere: "so dove abita".|
it:lei:pronoun||Lei, often written with a capital L, is also the polite "you", with the verb in the third person: "Lei è italiano?"
it:stare:verb||Stare is used for how you are and for staying: "come stai?", "sto a casa". Stare + gerund is an action in progress: "sto mangiando".
it:prego:interjection||Prego answers grazie (you're welcome), and also means "go ahead" or "pardon?".
it:ciao:interjection||Ciao means hello and goodbye among friends. With strangers use buongiorno or buonasera, and arrivederci.
it:fare:verb||Weather uses fare: "fa caldo", "fa freddo".
it:pretendere:verb|Pretendere means to demand or claim, not to pretend (fingere).|
it:caldo:adjective|Caldo means warm or hot, even though it looks like English "cold". Cold is freddo.|
it:burro:noun|Burro means butter. A donkey is "asino" (Spanish burro).|
it:annoiare:verb|Annoiare means to bore. To annoy is "dare fastidio" or "infastidire".|
it:ci:adverb||C'è means "there is", ci sono "there are".
